reasons: The overview shows two separate tent settlements and the top bar states two villages. The lower settlement is labelled village 1 (23), and the upper settlement village 2, from 1 (13).

The labels are small but their dark rectangular backing and placement above the tents make both identities and the 2-from-1 relationship readable at original image size. The night view also visibly identifies village 2 as from 1, with population 15.
People carry bundles, travel as a group and follow a dotted route toward a square destination marker away from the camp. The two views show the group first near the camp and then beyond the river.

The readable news line reports 13 people leaving village 1. These cues communicate a group moving away to settle. The destination settlement is not yet visible, so successful founding is not established by these walking images.
The moon, 02:00 time, winter text and cold counter reinforce a dark blue-green night scene. Pale frost-like accents on the tent tops and an unlit firepit make cold legible.
The tents, firepit, wood, bushes and tree stumps retain visible silhouettes despite the dim scene. No individual suffering or death event is visible in this screenshot.

The controlled calibration shows five distinct cross colors: brown, saturated blue, red, gray and pale blue. Brown is less prominent and gray versus pale blue is subtler, but all five are distinguishable against the displayed background.

All five cause descriptions are readable in the diagnostic list. The actual HUD displays its stated four-row limit with thirst, fighting, old age and freezing; starvation appears in the diagnostic list.
This is explicitly synthetic calibration, so this verdict does not claim natural death occurrence or terrain-background readability.
Inspected only the five supplied round-two image files using original-detail image viewing, with no crop or additional zoom.
The visible village count and lineage, group travel purpose, cold-night scene and controlled five-color calibration are readable within these screenshots.
Village text remains compact; acceptance is for the supplied original-size images, not smaller displays. No invisible simulation events were inferred as proven.
